public_rationale: The sources describe substantial debt exposure alongside equity participation. Neither establishes the proportion of AI compute purchases funded by debt in the relevant quarter. Rising borrowing does not establish almost-total debt funding, and evidence that equity exists does not quantify its contribution. The unspecified accounting basis also prevents a decisive financial comparison.
limitations: No numerical meaning is assigned to almost entirely.
Corporate cash is fungible, and financing can pass through several companies before paying for compute.
The available contextual evidence cannot establish either the claimed sector-wide share or its opposite.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Apparent demand for AI compute is almost entirely funded by debt.

statement.excerpt: That “demand” is almost-entirely funded by debt.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that borrowed money finances overwhelmingly most AI compute purchasing demand, with operating cash and equity making only a minor contribution.
The surrounding discussion concerns sector-wide demand, not merely the subset of projects financed through debt deals.
Because no period is named, use January through March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter that public company reports could cover before the post.
No numerical cutoff or accounting basis is supplied. Do not invent a percentage threshold or infer funding attribution from debt issuance alone.
criteria.support_condition: A representative, reconciled account of first-quarter AI compute purchases shows that debt financed overwhelmingly nearly all purchases, with only minor non-debt funding.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that operating cash or equity financed a substantial share of the same purchases, inconsistent with almost entirely debt funding.
